sourceInformation.tech: Three.js 0.180.0 (MIT; three.js authors); WebGPURenderer (WebGPU primary, WebGL2 compatibility); Rapier 0.19.3 (Apache-2.0; Dimforge); Gamepad API; Web Audio; WebRTC; AI Hub Session Protocol v1
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded jungle, flat-shaded color planes, black ink silhouettes and warm expedition typography
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClips for explorer locomotion, climbing, jumping and swinging; procedural wildlife and foliage
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-generated marimba music, percussion, ambience, effects and Animalese-style gibberish; music defaults to 10%
sourceInformation.online: 1–4 player ghost races through AI Hub; standalone nearby-tab rooms and manually paired WebRTC invitations
sourceInformation.testing: Input-only full expedition at default settings; headless simulation, emulated standard controller and multitouch, native WebGPU in virtual X display, compatibility renderer for multi-page WebRTC and AI Hub harness; audio signal metrics. Physical devices and listening unknown. Remote NAT traversal unknown.
sourceInformation.research: none; native source knowledge; supplied AI Hub integration files retrieved

testingFeedback: Eleven issues found through scripted checks, visual checks and integration review; all corrected: ghost positioning, small-screen title overlap, software graphics loss/stalls, results Back navigation, input after Hub end, touch ladder timing, exposed sky below caves, and phone canvas/HUD sizing during rotation, touch guide prompts, controller credits scrolling, and delayed Hub handshakes under load. Final combined suite: 138 checks passed, 0 failed.
Three could stop usable play: a lost/stalled graphics device, an empty results screen after Back, and a delayed Hub handshake under heavy load. No unresolved game-breaking issues.
The input-only default-settings playthrough collected all six relics, rode all three vines, explored both caves and reached the exit without teleports or cheats.
The first headless WebGPU screenshot was blank and could not judge the art; native WebGPU under virtual X and compatibility captures supplied useful visual evidence.
engineFeedback: Three.js makes procedural scenes and native clip animation straightforward; Rapier provides reliable character collisions.
The supplied software WebGPU adapter flag lost or stalled devices, even with two boxes. A Vulkan SwiftShader configuration rendered correctly; automatic WebGL2 recovery covers device loss and stalls.
The platforming state machine, vine attachment, level data, controller menus and multiplayer lifecycle.
Coordinating kinematic physics, vine motion and layered side-on composition.
A compact, first-party character-controller and gamepad-menu starter would reduce setup.
promptFeedback: The source, visual style, controller-first UX and explicit finished-demo requirements give a clear creative target.
No major ambiguity; standalone multiplayer needed a practical pairing design without a supplied signaling service.
Delivering traversal, rich procedural art, accessible input and two multiplayer transports in one offline HTML.
Specify whether standalone internet play should include hosted signaling or manual peer pairing.

aiHub.name: Pitfallin’
aiHub.tagline: A little danger. A lot of jungle.
aiHub.description: Swing through an ink-drawn jungle, hop crocodile jaws and explore beneath the roots. Find six lost sun relics before sunset, solo or alongside your friends’ racing ghosts.
aiHub.controls: A/D or left stick move; Space/Cross jump or release; E/Square catch vine; W/S or stick up/down climb; M/Triangle map; Esc/Options pause. Touch: left drag moves, right tap jumps, contextual action assists.
